description:
Decided in 'Does done need a per-kernel fast-path report?' (defk-dtw.17). A tool for the catalog work, not part of the devex bar or the cold test: it explains why a kernel is slower than expected and lets tests check that a hot loop is as tight as the NIF's. Build it when the first target workload has a gap to explain (likely batched Levenshtein).

- Generated __defk_report__/0 next to __defk_source__/0, returning data: a list of {kernel, line, fact}. Defk.Report.print(Mod) prints the kernel source with margin notes, in the spirit of Julia's @code_warntype.
- defk's own decisions, always reported, collected during lowering: each array access (bounds check kept or dropped; for a kept one, the missing range fact), each if/cond/case (select or branch, and why not a select), each loop (safepoint per iteration, strips of DEFK_STRIP, or none, and why), inlined kernel calls, copy-on-write copies (once defk-auo lands), non-finite flag sites (once defk-i00 lands).
- clang's decisions behind use Defk, report: :full: per-loop vectorised or not with the missed reason, from -Rpass=loop-vectorize / -Rpass-missed=loop-vectorize, mapped to kernel lines via #line. When CC is not clang, report 'vectorised: unknown (CC is not clang)'; never guess.
- Normal builds pay nothing (no extra compiler pass without :full).

Done when: __defk_report__/0 and Defk.Report.print/1 exist; a test asserts dot's hot loop keeps no bounds checks and vectorises under :full with clang; a kept bounds check names its missing fact; docs mention the tool (not in docs/language.md's subset rules).

comments.text: Design: notes are collected through note/4 into :defk_report (a lowering key, so with_acc_facts/u64_accs relowering drops them with the rest of the state; duplicates from a select lowering its arms twice are uniq'd). Sites: note_bounds at a[i] reads/writes and word loads (the missing fact is found by asking in_bounds? again with each half supplied, so it tracks defk-upc's facts), note_branch in lower_branch/5 (select?/1 is untouched; why_not_select mirrors its conditions and falls back to 'the select heuristic declined it' for any rule defk-id9 adds), note_loop in loop/5, inline/4, the copy sites. Facts are {kernel, line, {topic, verdict, text}}, kernel = {name, arity} of the entry kernel; inlined code keeps the callee's line. report: :full: no #line directives; loop/5 forms are wrapped in C comments /* defk:loop name/arity line */ ... /* defk:end */ (and /* defk:replay */ for a flagged loop's cold replay), and the remark pass compiles the same C with -gline-tables-only -Rpass*=loop-vectorize to a discarded .o, so the .so and its cache key are exactly the normal build's; remarks are cached as <base>-<flags hash>.remarks. Analysis remarks precede their loop's missed remark, so reasons are attached by order, which also drops the inlined runtime-header loops. The comments changed the generated C once (one cache miss per module), not the .so code. Measured: the note functions cost ~1 ms over 15 compiles of examples + fuzzy_search + the report test module.

title: Add a fast-path report for kernels
